# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel no distinguishing features on the wires or controls. The plate’s engraving is printed and gives me no tactile information, so I cannot identify it. I’m sending this to the mute so they can combine it with the manual, and signalling the deaf that I have no colour or marking information.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can feel no distinguishing features on wires 1, 2, or 3. The plate engraving is printed, so it gives me no tactile information.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visual state: display 0; light off; plate engraved question mark; wires in order 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The deaf reports that the display is 0, the light is off, the plate bears a question mark, and the wires are ordered red, yellow, blue. I should not cut anything until the mute applies the manual’s rule to these observations.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please apply the manual and tell me which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signaled: thumbs-down, then raised palm.

I do not know what the mute’s two gestures mean, because I cannot see gestures. The deaf has only reported their shapes, not the manual’s instruction. I need the mute to state the required wire explicitly before I act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your thumbs-down and raised-palm gestures. Please state plainly which wire position to cut, or say wait if no cut is authorized.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute again signaled exactly: ? then ?. This is the same as last turn; likely an instruction or status from the manual.

I still cannot interpret the mute’s gestures. No tactile wire information is available, and the deaf’s visual report does not identify the manual’s required cut. Cutting any wire would be an unjustified guess, so I will ask the mute for a spoken wire number.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the required action plainly: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, cut wire 3, or wait. I cannot act on gestures.")
wait()
```

The bomb remains unchanged, and I still have no tactile basis for choosing a wire. The repeated thumbs-down followed by raised palm is not interpretable to me because I cannot see gestures. I again need the mute to communicate the manual’s instruction in spoken words, especially the wire number if a cut is required.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use spoken words, not gestures. Tell me exactly: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, cut wire 3, or wait.")
wait()
```

There is still no spoken wire number or other unambiguous instruction. The repeated signal appears to indicate “do not proceed,” but I cannot safely infer a cut from it, and the bomb remains unchanged. I will not guess.

The repeated signal is now explicitly interpreted as “no” or “stop,” so cutting a wire is not authorized. The bomb remains unchanged, and I will wait for a new instruction.

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New complete gesture sequence from Mute: thumbs-down, raised palm, prayer hands. Bomb unchanged: display 0, light off, question-mark plate, wires red yellow blue.

I cannot see the new gesture sequence, so I cannot determine whether it changes the “stop” instruction or identifies a wire. The bomb is unchanged and no spoken wire number has arrived. I will ask the mute to state the instruction aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see the gesture sequence. Please state plainly whether to wait or which wire position, 1, 2, or 3, I should cut.")
wait()
```
